messages.content: You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
Beyond observing and approving, what new thing does the command console let the operator do?
The command console allows the operator to initiate a bounded runtime command.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What is the authority for what may be commanded, and what is the consoles' relationship to it?
The command registry is the authority. The consoles render the registry but do not define it; they cannot invent commands not listed in it or change how those commands are gated.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What are the three gates a command can carry?
The three gates are direct, approval, and forbidden.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What does the console add to the runtime's authority?
The console adds no new authority; it allows the operator to initiate a bounded runtime command rather than just reacting to one.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
An approval-gated command executes only after what?
An approval-gated command executes only after an operator approval confirmed by a device biometric.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
Why can a desktop console not complete a sensitive command on its own?

A desktop console cannot self-approve a sensitive action because only the mobile approve route records a biometric confirmation; the surface that asks is not allowed to be the same surface that consents.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What happens to an approval recorded by a channel that is not the mobile biometric route?
An approval recorded by any other channel is stored, but it does not release the command; the command remains in an "awaiting" state with a note indicating it is waiting.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
Which switch governs the console path, which governs the chat path, and which is on by default?
The **COMMAND_EXECUTION** switch governs the console path, while the **ENABLE_TOOL_EXECUTION** switch governs the model-initiated chat tool path. **COMMAND_EXECUTION** is on by default.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
Which command outcomes are written to the command log?
The command log records every outcome, including those that did not succeed: forbidden, denied, expired, and failed.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
Why does a read-only command execute immediately instead of waiting for an approval?
A read-only command executes immediately because it does not change state; it only observes and returns, meaning an approval would not protect anything.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
Under what condition will the console direct-run a bounded tool, and what happens otherwise?
The console will direct-run a bounded tool only when the tool declares no side effects. If a tool changes state (a side-effecting tool) and is offered as a direct command, it is refused, not run.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What is the first read-only direct command, and what does it read?
The first read-only direct command is **host_status**, which reads the host machine's CPU, memory, disk, and uptime.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What does the forbidden gate protect, and which registry command is forbidden?
The forbidden gate protects **Model Lock and output fidelity**. The forbidden command in the registry is **change_conversational_routing**.
You are 0M3-G4-ARC. Answer from your studied knowledge.
What must a destructive command have before it can qualify for the registry at all?
A destructive command must have an explicit undo before it can qualify at all.
